findings.message: Switching from nullish coalescing (??) to logical OR (||) changes behavior for valid falsy inputs. The requirement states a non-negative integer limit is valid including zero, and only null/undefined should select the default 20. With `limit || 20`, passing 0 returns 20 instead of 0, breaking the documented contract that zero disables processing. Also, `||` would coerce any other falsy value (though 0 is the documented case) to the default. Use `limit ?? 20` to preserve semantics.
